newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi says foreign-loan security rule under review.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi says foreign-loan security rule under review.

text.p: Vietnam's new minister of planning and investment, Nguyen Xuan Gia, said on Monday that legislation would be passed to allow forms of security on foreign loans other than the guarantee of a Vietnamese bank.

"Other forms of security will be established in the coming time in guidelines on implementing the law," Gia, who was promoted to minister in a cabinet reshuffle last week, told reporters during a break in a National Assembly meeting.
"Of course in the government we have some consensus about the extension of the forms of guarantee on foreign loans," he said.

A report in the Asia Times newspaper last month said the central bank had written to Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, informing him that all foreign loans in which pledges over assets or equity were offered as security were illegal.
It said the central bank had asked Kiet to find a way for enterprises to borrow from foreign lenders who require more than a bank guarantee as security, which is often seen by creditors as too risky.
Gia declined to give details of what other forms of guarantee would be allowed for foreign lenders.
Foreign bankers say that despite a reform drive, current legislation on foreign loan guarantees underlines the communist government's uneasiness about pledging land use rights or other local assets.
